newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS EDGE ORIOLES WITH NINTH INNING STRIKEOUTS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS EDGE ORIOLES WITH NINTH INNING STRIKEOUTS.

text.p: Ninth-inning, bases-loaded strikeouts of sluggers Eric Davis and Rafael Palmeiro by Mike Jackson and Alvin Morman preserved the Cleveland Indians' 7-6 victory over the Baltimore Orioles Sunday.
The Orioles had rallied for a pair of runs off Jackson in the top of the ninth to get within a run when Morman, a lefty, was summoned to get out Palmeiro, who bats left-handed.
On three pitches, Palmeiro swung and missed, fouled a ball off and struck out swinging to end the game.
"You get your heart racing a little bit, but you have to find a point where you calm down and make good pitches," Morman said.

"Al's got two saves and both have been in tough spots," said Cleveland manager Mike Hargrove. "He struck out Lee Stevens in Texas, but this one was probably even tougher. However, the bigger out was Mike Jackson's strikeout of Eric Davis."
Jackson had started the ninth and loaded the bases on a bunt single to B.J. Surhoff, a walk to Tony Tarasco and pinch-hitter Pete Incaviglia's infield single.
Jeff Reboulet ran for Incaviglia before Brady Anderson sliced a two-run double to make it 7-6. Roberto Alomar was walked intentionally and Jackson struck out Davis before giving way to Morman.

Palmeiro had stroked his ninth homer in the top of the sixth to tie it at 4-4, countering Justice's 14th homer which led off the fifth. Surhoff also homered for Baltimore and Sandy Alomar for Cleveland.

Charles Nagy (6-2) allowed four runs -- three earned -- and six hits with three walks and three strikeouts in seven innings to get the win. Arthur Rhodes (2-2), the second of four Baltimore pitchers, took the loss.
The Indians are 7-1 in their last eight games.
The start of the game was delayed for one hour, 45 minutes by rain.
In Kansas City, Chili Davis led off the bottom of the 11th with a homer off Bobby Ayala (3-2) to give the Royals a 4-3 victory over the Seattle Mariners.
Davis belted an 0-1 pitch out to right-centre to make a winner of Jamie Walker (3-2), who worked a scoreless 11th.
Ken Griffey Jr hit his major league-leading 22nd homer, a solo shot in the first, to tie his own major-league record for most home runs by the end of May, accomplished in 1994.
Joey Cora had an RBI single that extended his hitting streak to a career-best 20 games, keeping him even with Chicago's Albert Belle for the longest streak in the majors this season.
In Toronto, Benito Santiago drew a bases-loaded walk from Rich DeLucia with no outs in the 11th as the Blue Jays benefitted from a fluke play and beat the Anaheim Angels 4-3.

DeLucia (4-2), who came in to start the 10th, allowed Ed Sprague to loft what appeared to be a routine fly ball into right-centre field. Centre fielder Jim Edmonds and right fielder Tim Salmon looked at each other and let the ball drop.
While Edmonds appeared to yell at Salmon, the ball rolled to the wall and Sprague ended up with a triple.
DeLucia then issued intentional walks to Carlos Delgado and Ruben Sierra before Juan Samuel pinch-ran for Sprague. Santiago walked on a full count, sending in the winning run.
Mike Timlin (1-0), the fourth Toronto pitcher, blew his third save in eight chances but held on for the win.

In Chicago, Jeff Cirillo had a career-high four RBI and his two-run single in the fourth inning snapped a tie as the Milwaukee Brewers outslugged the White Sox 11-7 in the rubber game of their three-game series.
Milwaukee, which climbed back to the .500 mark at 22-22, won for just the third time in its last 11 games.
Belle extended his hitting streak to 20 games with a three-run homer in the first inning. The streak is one shy of his career high, established last season with the Indians.

In Detroit, Bob Higginson went 4-for-5, including his second career grand slam, and Felipe Lira (3-2) pitched five innings for his third straight win as the Detroit Tigers posted a 13-5 victory over the Texas Rangers.
Bob Hamelin belted a two-run homer off Bobby Witt (7-1) in the second and scored in the fourth on a triple by Raul Casanova. Warren Newson hit two solo homers and Will Clark a two-run shot for Texas.
At Minnesota, Rich Becker's single off Billy Taylor (1-3) with two outs in the bottom of the 10th scored pinch-runner Matt Lawton with the winning run as the Twins beat the Oakland Athletics 7-6.
Rick Aguilera (2-1), the sixth Minnesota pitcher, got the win despite blowing a save for the fourth time this season. He allowed two runs and two hits in two innings.
Darrin Jackson and Pat Meares homered for Minnesota, while Mark McGwire and Geronimo Berroa connected for the Athletics.
In New York, the game between the Boston Red Sox and Yankees was postponed due to rain. No new date was announced.
